assetType: iOS/Android adaptive mobile app screen comp
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: iOS/Android adaptive mobile app screen comp for an Animal Crossing New Horizons diary app
Primary request: Create a high-fidelity portrait mobile UI mockup for the Korean "주민" resident list screen where users can update all five resident status records directly inside each resident card, without relying on a bottom sheet.
Surface structure: iPhone-style status bar; top app header with small island selector; large title "주민"; search row; compact icon category rail; then a vertically scrolling one-column list of resident cards. Each card has a large resident portrait on the left, resident name and two small trait chips in the center, and five large 48dp icon status controls in a horizontal row or wrapped two-row grid inside the card: 위시, 우리 섬, 이사, 캠핑, 액자. Selected controls show filled color and checkmark; unselected controls are soft outlined. A small chevron/detail button remains for optional detailed editing.
Interaction framing: The screen should clearly communicate that status recording happens directly on the list. No bottom sheet. No modal. No tiny tap targets. Reduce explanatory text; use icon-first controls with short Korean labels only where needed.
Style/medium: polished native mobile UI mockup, NookPhone-inspired original interface, warm tactile paper surface, soft rounded cards, gentle shadows, ACNH-like friendly iconography and character portrait placeholders, but not a screenshot from the game.
Color palette: warm paper ivory background, leaf green primary, resident coral, catalog amber, museum blue, soft neutral brown ink.
Typography: Korean mobile UI, bold clear headings, compact labels, no negative letter spacing.
Text (verbatim where visible): "주민", "햇살 섬", "주민 이름으로 검색", "전체", "위시", "우리 섬", "이사", "캠핑", "액자", "잭슨", "쭈니", "미애".
Constraints: portrait 390x844 style composition; all controls visually at least 44pt/48dp; one resident per row; no bottom sheet; no modal; no tiny tap targets; no instructional text blocks; no marketing hero; no nested cards; accessible spacing; show selected and unselected states clearly by shape plus color.
Avoid: tiny icon-only buttons with no state affordance, dense two-column cards, bottom sheet, long explanatory copy, purple-blue dominant palette, dark theme, web dashboard layout, stock-photo look, Nintendo logos or game UI screenshots.
